surveyMeta.description: An async choose-your-own-adventure for Britt's world building, character development, and lore discovery.
surveyMeta.title: Britt's Afternoon Out
surveyMeta.name: Britt's Afternoon Out

blocks.content: Before the intense Curfew & study cramming of Wednesday night, you have a free afternoon. The dry air of Harmony Prime is dusty, and the communal dorms of Block 04 feel sterile. You need to get out, explore, and find answers about what Harmony really wants with the Mizizi.
Where would you like to go?

ports.subtext: Smoky, crowded, and loud. The beating heart of the lower city.
Workshop spires smelling of grease and copper. High-end tools.
The basalt cliffs and lower basin runoff, where the wilderness pushes back.
The Gilded Spires and Sterling airship decks. Floating gardens and wealth.

blocks.content: Steam vents hiss rhythmically in the narrow stone alleys. You pass stalls selling roasted meats, imported spices, and minor copper machinery. Suddenly, a malfunctioning automated steam-harvester clanks and screeches, venting hot pressure. The crowd gasps and steps back.

ports.subtext: Step back and help a nearby vendor, Ma'o, pick up a tray of spilled pastries.
Dart closer to inspect the pressure valves. Maybe you can salvage a regulator?
Watch the enforcers' patrol routes and note the crowd's reaction to authority.

blocks.content: You help Ma'o, an old, dusty dwarf baker, gather his spiced Sun-Cakes. He wipes his brow and sighs: 'Thank you, Green-Back. The enforcers' high-frequency sweeps have been making all the automated tech act up lately. Vumbua is pushing the grid too hard.'
He hands you a warm, honey-spiced Sun-Cake: 'On the house. Good luck to you forest folk.'

ports.subtext: You gained a warm pastry and a friendly connection to Ma'o.

blocks.content: You duck under the venting steam, your sturdy shell shielding you from the heat. You reach for the copper regulator spring inside the harvester's casing before the Indigo Turbans arrive to cordon it off. Add your Finesse modifier to the roll!

outcomes.label: Failure! A blast of hot steam!

blocks.content: You wait for the perfect moment. As the steam vents hiss a rhythmic break, you dart in, slide the latch open, and snatch the copper regulator spring from the automated harvester's casing.
You slip back into the crowd just as two Indigo Turbans arrive to cordon off the area. You got the regulator!

ports.subtext: Secure your new loot.

blocks.content: You misjudge the rhythm of the steam. As you reach inside the casing, a sudden high-pressure release of boiling steam vents directly onto your hand.
You cry out and pull back, your tough shell taking the brunt of the heat but leaving you parched and shaken (2 Stress). You have to retreat empty-handed before the guards spot you.

ports.subtext: Nursing your scalded hand.

blocks.content: You stay back, pulling your collar up. Two Indigo Turbans arrive and strike their tuning forks. The harvester's engine immediately whines and shuts down, matching the fork's pitch.

You notice that the crowd doesn't look relieved; they look resentful. You also catch that the enforcers' badges are stamped with a seal from the High Spires—meaning they are dispatched directly from the council, not local precincts.

ports.subtext: You memorize the pattern of their harmonic shut-off.

blocks.content: You enter a cramped brass workshop smelling of copper and grease. The shopkeeper, an off-duty gnome clerk named Tommy, is struggling with a broken steam-alignment gauge. His workbench is cluttered with blueprints and clockwork parts.

ports.subtext: Strike up a friendly conversation and help him find a dropped copper screw.
Slip into the back room to check the node connector shipment.
Silently watch his mechanical force and compare it to how Mizizi shape wooden nodes.

blocks.content: You spot the screw wedged under a toolbox. Tommy beams: 'Ah! Lifesaver! I'm so stressed about the Logistics exam on Friday, my hands are shaking. If we don't help each other out, the Loom wins, right?'
He pulls out a hand-drawn map: 'Here, it's a Clerk's Map of the Spire-Scape. Shows the quietest dead-zones where the steam pipes don't hiss. Great for hiding out or studying.'

ports.subtext: You gained a map and a friendly classmate.

blocks.content: You slip into the store's back room storage area. Instead of blueprints, you happen to see Professor Kante, who is out shopping for new node connectors. Add your Knowledge modifier to the roll to stay hidden and overhear his muttering!

outcomes.label: Failure! Caught in the back room!

blocks.content: You stay perfectly still behind a shelf of copper pipes. You hear Professor Kante muttering: 'Never... I'm never going to understand why the Ash-Blood node is underpowered. 20 amps instead of 300? It doesn't make mechanical sense...'
He shakes his head in frustration, sets down a small set of pocket mechanic tools he was holding, and exits the room. You slip out of hiding and pocket the tools!

ports.subtext: You have pocketed Kante's dropped tools.

blocks.content: You try to squeeze behind a stack of brass pipes, but your sturdy shell bumps them. A loud metallic clatter rings through the back room.

Professor Kante and Tommy turn around immediately. Tommy spots you: 'Oh, sorry, student! This area is off-limits.' Kante looks at you suspiciously before Tommy politely but firmly ushers you back to the front desk. You left empty-handed and stressed (2 Stress).

ports.subtext: Exiting quickly.

blocks.content: You watch Tommy clamp a brass piston into place, applying heavy tension until the gears lock. Harmony's technology is built on forced alignment. They bend, shape, and lock materials to execute their will.

This is completely opposite to Mizizi nodes, which are grown over decades, utilizing the natural curves of wood and mycelium webs to guide energy without force. You realize Harmony's design is inherently fragile—if the tension slips, the whole system collapses.

ports.text: Leave the shop with these insights
ports.subtext: You understand the fundamental flaw in their engineering.

blocks.content: You follow a runoff pipe to the outer basalt cliffs. The city's massive structure looms behind you, venting hot steam. Here, the wild forests of the valley push back. Below the cliff, you spot a wild patch of iridescent fungal nodes and an old, abandoned research cache.

ports.subtext: Sit on the cliff edge and share some trail food with a tired wilderness scout, Grip.
Climb down the wet, slippery basalt face to crack open the abandoned cache.
Study how the chemical runoff from the city's pipes affects the wild fungal growth below.

blocks.content: You share some dried moss-bread with Grip. He rests his boots and looks out: 'The city's growing, but the valley is still wild. I've tracked some terrifying aether beasts in other forests of this size. Especially one outside the ruined civilization down south that nearly destroyed my old airship. A real nightmare.'

He chuckles, looking distant: 'Though my captain back then was a madman who thought he could catch it. Anyway, found this in the basin. Wipes clean and helps look through the mist. Take it, Green-Back.'

ports.subtext: You gained a Focus Glass piece and stories of the wilds.

blocks.content: The basalt is slick with oil runoff. You attempt to scale down, using your shell to brace against the narrow cracks. Add your Agility modifier to the roll!
You climb down surely, your root-kin feet finding traction on the basalt. You reach the ledge and pry open the rusty latch of the surveyor's cache.
Inside, you find a pristine surveyor's compass in a leather pouch! You slip it into your bag and scale back up to the main path.

ports.subtext: You secured the surveyor's compass.

blocks.content: As you reach for a handhold, a patch of slick algae gives way under your fingers. You slide ten feet down the wet basalt, scraping your shell loudly before catching yourself on a lower ledge.
The impact leaves you bruised and shaken (2 Stress). The cache is out of reach, and you have to climb back up empty-handed.

ports.subtext: Dusting yourself off.

blocks.content: You inspect the fungal patch below the pipes. The mycelium is thick, but it is a sickly grey-brown. The chemical discharge from the city's power plant is draining the life, making the mushrooms grow in rigid, stunted patterns rather than spreading naturally.
It matches what is happening to the Petrified Forest back home. Harmony's integration isn't a trade; it's a slow leak. They are draining the surrounding lands to feed the Spires.

ports.subtext: You have proof of the city's impact.

blocks.content: You climb the central elevators to the floating gardens of the Gilded Spires. The air smells of jasmine and high-grade oil. Servants walk past carrying glasses of sparkling wine. A pre-race reception is underway, filled with noble captains and Grand Architects.

ports.subtext: Use your Gold student status to join a conversation with a friendly noble assistant.
Sneak near the private balcony railing to eavesdrop on two Grand Architects.
Stand at the edge of the platform and trace the physical pipelines of power down the Spires.

blocks.content: You act natural, snacking on luxury fruit. A young captain's assistant strikes up a chat, amused by a root-kin on the Gilded deck: 'Ah, a Vumbua candidate! Everyone is talking about the Sterling ship's custom Vox capacitor. If they win tomorrow, the Sterling family will double their holdings in the Lower Basin.'
She hands you a small Sterling family emblem pin: 'For luck. Try to bet on them if you can.'

ports.subtext: You gained an emblem pin and political gossip.

blocks.content: You blend into the shadow of a marble pillar, focusing your senses on the hushed conversation of the two architects. Add your Instinct modifier to the roll!

You stay hidden in the shadows. You hear the two architects debating the Mizizi integration. One whispers: 'The elders think it's a simple alignment of roots, but our calculations show the sync is mystical. It requires a synchronization of life and death—a baby born in the Petrified Forest and a baby born in Harmony Prime at the exact same moment someone dies.'
The other replies: 'Absurd. Life and death in perfect balance? That's too volatile.' They walk away, leaving a Sterling Ledger on a nearby chair. You quickly pocket it!

ports.subtext: You secured the Sterling ledger.

blocks.content: You try to lean closer, but a servant carrying a tray of wine glasses bumps into your sturdy shell. The glass clatters, drawing the attention of the architects.

A Gilded guard immediately approaches: 'Pardon me, candidate, but this platform is reserved for captains and guests.' He politely but firmly escorts you back to the public elevator. The embarrassment leaves you stressed (2 Stress).

ports.subtext: Stepping into the elevator.

blocks.content: Standing at the gilded railing, you look down. The city is a vertical machine. Thick copper cables and glowing conduit pipes run from the smoky, noisy slums of Block 99 directly up to the floating decks of the Gilded Spires.

You realize that the clean air, the jasmine scents, and the bright crystal lights here are literally siphoned from the sweat and blood of the workers below. Harmony isn't creating power; they are transferring it upwards.

ports.subtext: You see the system clearly now.

blocks.content: As you head back to the Block 04 dorms, you slip through a side alley to avoid the main patrol. Ahead, you spot Finch Gable—Lomi's arrogant rival candidate—whispering to an Indigo Turban enforcer.

You sneak closer and listen. Finch is trying to offer the guard information about Valerius Sterling in exchange for secure access to the Hangar Bay, so he can spy on what the second-years are building for the Reso Race.
How do you handle this?

ports.subtext: Kick a loose brass pipe to make a loud noise, hoping they drop something.
Let Finch leave, and follow the enforcer to see where he takes the bag.
Stay hidden, memorize the enforcer's badge number and the symbol on the satchel.

blocks.content: You kick a loose brass pipe. It clatters loudly down the stone steps. The enforcer jumps, dropping a folded sheet of parchment from the satchel before they both look around.

You immediately retreat into your shell, blending into the soot-stained bricks. Finch mutters: 'We're being watched, get moving.' Once they leave, you grab the dropped parchment: it's a cargo manifest showing a delivery of a 'Dissonant Fungal Core' to Hangar Gantry, Bay 4. This is a crucial clue about the missing Ash-Blood node!

ports.subtext: Slip back into Block 04 before curfew.

blocks.content: You quietly tail the enforcer through the winding corridors. He heads toward the high-security Gantry level of the hangar bay. He passes a secure locker room and speaks to a guard: 'Valerius's team won't find their replacement node. The Warden has it locked in Bay 4.'
You memorize the locker location. This is a critical lead! You slip back to your room before the guard spots you.

ports.subtext: Slip back into Block 04 before curfew.

blocks.content: You stay perfectly still in the dark. The enforcer's badge number is **449**. The satchel is stamped with the Sterling family crest, but with a black line drawn through it.

You hear Finch whisper: 'Tell Warden Rovaldi that the replacement node is secured. Valerius has no idea his rig is compromised.' This links the missing node directly to Warden Rovaldi! You slip away quietly with this name and badge.

ports.subtext: Slip back into Block 04 before curfew.

blocks.content: You slip back into your dorm room in Block 04 just as the Indigo Turbans strike their curfew bells outside. Aggie looks up, relieved to see you back safe.

ports.subtext: Rest and await Session 6.

blocks.content: You have completed your afternoon out. Await the start of Session 6.
